claims.text: The unit's record trail is continuous and official. The National Archives catalogue holds Operations Record Books for the Joint Air Reconnaissance Intelligence Centre (United Kingdom) from AIR 29/1361, RAF Station Nuneham Park, September to December 1950, to AIR 29/5764, RAF Brampton, 1992, in the series 'Air Ministry and Ministry of Defence: Operations Record Books, Miscellaneous Units', with 'JARIC (UK): administrative history', 1962-1972, at AIR 14/4103.

claims.text: The Ministry of Defence UFO reports file covering the Calvine period is closed for another fifty years. DEFE 24/1940, 'UFO reports', 1 August 1990 to 31 January 1991, former reference D/Sec(AS)12/2 Part J, is held at Kew as a Public Record with closure code 84 under the closure criterion 'Personal information where the applicant is a 3rd party', a Freedom of Information Act exemption signed 7 June 2023, and a record opening date of 1 January 2076.

claims.text: On AREA52 - DEBRIEFED with Chris Ramsay, episode 34, 18 April 2025, at 1:25:17, Nick Pope said of the Calvine photographs: 'we had access to Jarrick, which was the joint air reconnaissance and intelligence center ... They looked at all this and they said, yeah, it's real. It's whatever it is. It's 75 feet across. It's a solid, structured craft, but we have no idea what it is.' At 1:26:06 he called it 'an official intelligence community analysis'. No JARIC assessment of these photographs has been opened, and the Ministry of Defence file covering the period is closed until 2076.

desc: JARIC is the United Kingdom's joint imagery-intelligence unit, and its institutional life is documented at The National Archives without reference to any UFO case: Operations Record Books run from RAF Nuneham Park in 1950 through RAF Brampton in 1992 in the Air Ministry and Ministry of Defence series, with an administrative history for 1962-1972 at AIR 14/4103. It reaches this board because Nick Pope says JARIC assessed the six Calvine photographs and their negatives and concluded the object was a solid structured craft about 75 feet across. No such assessment has been opened. The Defence Secretariat file covering the period, DEFE 24/1940, is closed at Kew until 1 January 2076 under a Freedom of Information Act exemption signed on 7 June 2023, on the same personal-information ground as every neighbouring file in the run; a redacted digital copy, DEFE 24/1940/1, has been open since 20 October 2008 and could not be downloaded from this environment.
